comments.author: @gmfv125
comments.text: While the capitalist United States is not necessarily a bad country to live in, it feels underdeveloped when compared to the exceptionally high standard of social welfare in Nordic European democracies. That enormous difference, especially in health, education, family, and working life, is brought about by integrating socialist-inspired policies into their capitalist economic and political systems. These are the same policies advocated by Bernie Sanders in the USA—a country so rich that, had he been elected president, the US would by now be enjoying the same exceptionally high living standards as the Nordic countries, or perhaps even better ones.

replies.author: @gmfv125
replies.text: @Beyondhorizon-n6t Everywhere, human beings by nature place high value on personal well-being, regardless of political, economic, or cultural differences.

replies.author: @Beyondhorizon-n6t
replies.text: Thank you for this very interesting comment. Nordic countries are often described as market-based economies with strong social welfare systems, and that combination has produced results that many people around the world admire. At the same time, political, economic, and cultural differences make it difficult to say with certainty what would happen if the same policies were adopted elsewhere.
